disposition_reason: Cadmium, zinc and lead were measured in palm weevil larvae and winged termites collected in Ijebu division, Ogun State, Nigeria, at collection and after 3 months of storage; Table 4 prints one value per insect and time point.

study.design: Field collection of two edible insects with a 3-month storage comparison
study.origin: wild-collected in six Local Government Areas (18 towns) of Ijebu division, Ogun State, Nigeria
study.method: AOAC (2003) methods; instrument and digestion not stated
study.qa: No CRM, recovery or blank reported

findings.group: initial reading, freshly caught, Ijebu division (Ogun State)
findings.notes: One value per insect and time point; replicate count and number of insects pooled not stated. Insects were sun dried before analysis, but the table basis is not labelled. Lead near 40 mg/kg and cadmium near 11-13 mg/kg are very high for food; the analytical technique is given only as AOAC (2003) methods.

unresolved: Analytical instrument, digestion, LOD and replicate count are not reported.
The abstract quotes the after-storage values (Cd 10.95/12.70, Zn 5.50/2.70, Pb 39.55/40.15 mg/kg) as if they were the study result; the table gives initial values too.
Basis (dry or fresh weight) of Table 4 is not stated; insects were sun dried.
source_record_corrections: Printed issue is Journal of Biology and Life Science 2013, Vol. 4, No. 1, pp. 18-23 (received August 2012); manifest year 2012.
